title: Abgoosht (Iranian lamb, chickpea and potato stew)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or shanks, on the bone

steps: Put the lamb, drained chickpeas and beans, onion, turmeric and water in a large pot and bring to the boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the meat and legumes are nearly tender.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, whole potatoes and dried limes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for another 45 minutes.
Lift out the meat, potatoes and some of the chickpeas, and mash them together with a heavy pestle or potato masher, discarding bones, to make a thick paste.
Serve the broth first with torn flatbread, then the mashed meat and fresh herbs, onion and pickles on the side.

title: Albaloo polo (Iranian sour cherry rice with chicken)

ingredients.name: dried sour cherries (or pitted canned sour cherries, drained)
saffron, ground and steeped in hot water

steps: Simmer the chicken with the onion, turmeric, salt, pepper and a cup of water for about 40 minutes until tender, then keep the pieces warm.
Cook the cherries with the sugar and 3 tablespoons of water over low heat for 15 minutes until syrupy, taking care not to burn them.
Parboil the rice in well salted water for 6 minutes, drain, and rinse briefly.
Heat oil in a pot, add a base layer of rice, then layer rice and cherries alternately, saving a few cherries for garnish.
Drizzle with the saffron water and the remaining oil, cover with a towel-wrapped lid, and steam on low for 40 minutes.
Serve the rice topped with the saved cherries, with the chicken alongside.

title: Ash reshteh (Iranian noodle, herb and bean soup)

ingredients.name: dried kidney beans or pinto beans, soaked overnight
mixed fresh parsley, coriander, spinach and dill, chopped
kashk (or sour cream thinned with a little lemon juice)

steps: Boil the soaked chickpeas and beans in the water with half the onion and the turmeric for about 1 hour until beginning to soften.
Add the lentils and cook for 20 minutes more.
Stir in the chopped herbs and season with salt and pepper, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook for about 10 minutes until tender, stirring so they do not clump together.
Fry the remaining onion in the oil until deep golden brown and keep some for garnish.
Serve the soup in bowls and top with a swirl of kashk or sour cream and the fried onion.

title: Ash-e doogh (Iranian yogurt, herb and rice soup)

ingredients.name: mixed fresh herbs (spinach, parsley, coriander, dill, chives), chopped

steps: Bring the water to the boil, add the rice and chickpeas, and simmer for 20 minutes until the rice is soft.
Whisk the yogurt, flour and egg yolk together until smooth, then temper it by whisking in a ladleful of the hot liquid.
Pour the yogurt mixture slowly into the pot, stirring constantly in one direction so it does not split, and cook gently for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped herbs and salt and simmer for 15 more minutes without boiling hard.
Fry the onion in the oil until golden, stir in the dried mint for a few seconds, and spoon this over each serving.

title: Baghali polo (Iranian dill and broad bean rice)

ingredients.name: shelled broad (fava) beans, fresh or frozen, peeled
fresh dill, finely chopped (or 3 tbsp dried)
saffron, ground and steeped in 3 tbsp hot water

steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the salt, add the drained rice, and boil for 5 to 6 minutes until almost tender but still firm in the centre.
Add the broad beans for the last 2 minutes, then drain everything in a colander.
Heat half the butter or oil with 3 tablespoons of water in the pot and cover the base with a layer of rice if you want a crispy bottom.
Gently layer the rice, beans and dill in a pyramid, alternating them, and make a few holes down to the base with a spoon handle.
Dot with the remaining butter, wrap the lid in a clean tea towel, cover tightly, and cook on high for 5 minutes, then on low for 40 minutes.
Mix a few spoonfuls of rice with the saffron water for garnish and serve the rest with its crust of golden tahdig.

title: Barbari bread (Iranian long flatbread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and warm water into a soft, slightly sticky dough and knead for 10 minutes. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1.5 hours.
Whisk the extra flour with the 200 ml water in a small pan and heat until it thickens slightly into a thin glaze, then cool it.
Divide the dough into 2 or 3 pieces, shape into long ovals, and rest for 15 minutes on a floured surface.
Stretch each piece to about 35 cm, dimple it lengthwise with your fingers, brush with the glaze, and sprinkle with seeds.
Bake on a preheated tray at 240 C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Serve warm with feta, herbs, walnuts or butter and jam for breakfast.

title: Borani esfenaj (Iranian spinach and yogurt dip)
steps: Soften the onion in the oil over medium heat until golden.
Add the spinach in batches and cook until wilted and most of its liquid has evaporated.
Chop the cooked spinach finely and let it cool completely.
Mix the yogurt with the garlic, salt and pepper and stir in the cooled spinach and onion.
Chill for an hour so the flavours blend, then garnish with walnuts and serve with flatbread.

title: Faloodeh (Iranian rose and noodle sorbet)

ingredients.name: lime, cut in wedges, for serving

steps: Dissolve the sugar in the water over low heat, simmer for 5 minutes, and let it cool, then stir in the rosewater.
Cook the vermicelli in boiling water until tender, drain, rinse in cold water, and cut into short lengths.
Mix the noodles into the cooled syrup and pour into a shallow container.
Freeze for 2 hours, then break up the ice crystals with a fork, and repeat every 45 minutes until a granular, slushy ice forms, about 4 hours total.
Scoop into bowls, add a squeeze of lime juice, and a drizzle of sour cherry syrup if you like.

title: Fesenjan (Iranian pomegranate and walnut chicken stew)

ingredients.name: chicken thighs and drumsticks, skin on
pomegranate molasses (use more if it is mild)
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for a few minutes until fragrant, taking care not to scorch them, then let them cool.
Grind the walnuts in a food processor to a fine, slightly oily meal.
Soften the onions in the oil over medium heat until golden, then stir in the turmeric and add the chicken pieces. Turn them until lightly browned on all sides and season with salt and pepper.
Add the ground walnuts and the hot water or stock, stir well, cover, and simmer very gently for 45 minutes, stirring from time to time so the nuts do not catch on the bottom.
Pour in the pomegranate molasses and sugar and continue simmering, partly covered, for another 30 to 40 minutes until the sauce is thick, dark and glossy and the chicken is tender.
Taste and balance the sweet and sour, adding a little more sugar or molasses as needed, and serve with plain steamed rice.

title: Gheimeh (Iranian split pea and lamb stew with dried limes)

ingredients.name: lamb or beef stew meat, cut into small cubes
dried limes, pierced (or the juice of 1 lemon)

steps: Soak the split peas in cold water for an hour, then drain them.
Brown the onion in 2 tablespoons of the oil until soft and golden, add the turmeric, then add the meat and cook until it loses its raw colour.
Stir in the tomato paste and cinnamon and fry for a minute, then pour in the hot water and season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 45 minutes, then add the split peas and the pierced dried limes and cook for a further 40 minutes until the meat and peas are tender.
Meanwhile fry the potato fries in the remaining oil until golden and crisp and sprinkle with salt.
Taste the stew and adjust the sourness and salt, then spoon it over rice and top with the fried potatoes just before serving.

title: Jujeh kabab (Iranian saffron chicken kebab)

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thighs, cut into large chunks
saffron threads, ground and steeped in 3 tbsp hot water

steps: Whisk together the grated onion with its juice, yogurt, lemon juice, half the saffron water, oil, salt and pepper.
Add the chicken and turn to coat, then marinate in the fridge for at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.
Thread the chicken onto skewers, leaving a little space between pieces.
Grill over hot coals or under a grill for 12 to 15 minutes, turning often, until golden at the edges and cooked through.
Brush the cooked kebabs with the rest of the saffron water and butter if you like, and grill the tomatoes until blistered.
Serve with saffron rice and the grilled tomatoes.

title: Kabab koobideh (Iranian minced meat skewers)

ingredients.name: ground lamb, or half lamb and half beef, not too lean
large onion, grated and squeezed dry
saffron, ground and steeped in a little hot water, for brushing

steps: Mix the meat with the grated onion, salt, pepper and turmeric, then knead it firmly for about 8 minutes until the mixture becomes sticky and smooth.
Cover and chill for at least an hour so the mixture firms up.
Wet your hands, take a fistful of meat, and press it around a flat wide skewer into a long thin sausage, making finger dents along its length.
Grill over hot charcoal or under a very hot grill for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once or twice, until browned and just cooked through. Grill the tomatoes at the same time.
Brush the kebabs with the saffron water while still hot.
Serve on rice or flatbread with the blistered tomatoes and a sprinkle of sumac.

title: Kabab torsh (Gilan sour walnut and pomegranate kebab)

ingredients.name: beef or lamb tenderloin, in thin strips or small cubes
fresh parsley and mint, finely chopped

steps: Mix the ground walnuts, pomegranate molasses, garlic, herbs, grated onion, oil, salt and pepper into a thick marinade.
Coat the meat thoroughly with the marinade, cover, and leave in the fridge for 8 to 24 hours.
Thread the meat onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until the meat is cooked through but still juicy.
Serve hot with rice or flatbread and fresh herbs.

title: Kashk-e bademjan (Iranian aubergine dip with whey)

ingredients.name: kashk (or thick Greek yogurt with a little salt)

steps: Salt the aubergine slices and let them sweat for 20 minutes, then pat them dry and fry in oil until golden and soft.
Fry the onions slowly in the same pan until deep golden, reserving a spoonful for garnish.
Fry the garlic for 1 minute and stir in the turmeric.
Add the aubergines and a splash of water, then mash everything together into a rough paste and warm it through.
Stir in most of the kashk, season, and adjust to taste.
Warm the dried mint in a little oil for a few seconds. Serve the dip topped with the fried onion, mint oil, extra kashk and walnuts, with flatbread.

title: Khoresh bademjan (Iranian aubergine and lamb stew)

ingredients.name: lamb or beef stew meat, cubed
pinch of saffron, ground and steeped in 2 tbsp hot water

steps: Peel the aubergines in stripes, cut them lengthwise into thick slices, salt them and leave for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry the aubergine slices in oil in batches until golden on both sides and drain on paper towels.
Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons of oil until golden, add the turmeric and the meat, and brown it lightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the tomato paste, add enough hot water to just cover the meat, and simmer covered for about 1 hour until the meat is tender.
Fry the tomato halves briefly and tuck them with the aubergine slices into the stew, then add the verjuice and saffron.
Cover and cook very gently for 20 minutes without stirring, so the aubergine stays in neat pieces, then serve with rice.

title: Khoresh karafs (Iranian celery and herb stew)

ingredients.name: lamb or beef stew meat, cubed
celery stalks (about 6 large), sliced 1 cm thick

steps: Fry the onion in 2 tablespoons of oil until golden, stir in the turmeric, and add the meat. Brown it, season, and add enough water to cover.
Cover and simmer for about 1 hour until the meat is nearly tender.
In a separate pan, fry the parsley and mint in the remaining oil over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until they darken and smell deeply of herbs.
Fry the celery slices briefly in the same pan, then add everything to the meat.
Pour in the lime or lemon juice, adjust the salt, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes until the celery is soft and the sauce has thickened.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Kuku sabzi (Persian herb frittata)

ingredients.name: spring onions or chives, finely chopped

steps: Beat the eggs in a large bowl with the turmeric, flour, baking powder, salt and pepper until well mixed.
Fold in the herbs, spring onions, walnuts and barberries so the mixture is mostly green.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in the mixture, spreading it evenly.
Cover and cook on low heat for about 12 minutes until the bottom is golden and the top is nearly set.
Cut into wedges, flip each piece (or turn the whole kuku using a plate) and cook the other side for 5 minutes.
Serve warm or at room temperature with flatbread, yogurt and fresh herbs.

title: Loobia polo (Iranian green bean, beef and tomato rice)

ingredients.name: beef or lamb, cut into small cubes
green beans, cut into 2 cm pieces
saffron, ground and steeped in hot water

steps: Fry the onion in half the oil until golden, add the turmeric and the meat, and brown it well.
Add the tomato paste, cinnamon, salt, pepper and enough water to cover, then simmer for about 45 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the green beans and cook for 10 minutes until just tender, leaving a thick, not watery, sauce.
Parboil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes and drain it.
Heat the remaining oil in a pot, spread a layer of rice on the bottom, then layer in the meat sauce and rice alternately, ending with rice.
Drizzle with saffron water, cover with a towel-wrapped lid, and steam on low for 40 minutes.

title: Mirza ghassemi (Iranian smoked aubergine and egg dip)

ingredients.name: ripe tomatoes, grated or finely chopped

steps: Prick the aubergines and char them over a flame, under a hot grill or in a very hot oven until the skin blackens and the flesh is soft.
Cool them slightly, peel off the skin, and mash the flesh with a fork.
Fry the garlic in the oil for a minute with the turmeric, add the tomatoes, and cook until the juices reduce.
Stir in the mashed aubergine, season with salt and pepper, and cook for about 10 minutes until thick.
Make a well, crack in the eggs, and stir them quickly through until just set.
Serve warm with flatbread or rice.

title: Nan-e berenji (Iranian rice flour cookies)
steps: Beat the butter and sugar together until pale and creamy, then add the egg yolk, rosewater and cardamom.
Sift in the rice flour and mix until it forms a soft dough, adding a teaspoon of milk if too dry.
Wrap and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll small balls of dough, flatten each slightly on a lined tray, and press a poppy seed pattern on top.
Bake at 160 C for 15 to 18 minutes until firm but still pale.
Let the cookies cool on the tray, as they are fragile when warm.

title: Sabzi polo (Iranian herb rice)

ingredients.name: chives or spring onion greens, finely chopped
saffron, ground and steeped in hot water

steps: Parboil the rice in salted water for 5 to 6 minutes until firm in the centre, then drain.
Heat some butter or oil in a heavy pot with a spoonful of water, and make a base layer of rice.
Mix the chopped herbs and garlic into the rest of the rice gently with a fork and pile it into the pot in layers, shaping a mound.
Poke a few steam holes through the rice, drizzle with remaining melted butter and 2 tablespoons water.
Cover with a towel-wrapped lid and cook on medium for 5 minutes, then on low for 40 minutes.
Serve topped with a spoonful of saffron rice and the crisp golden tahdig, traditionally with fried fish on Nowruz.

title: Salad Shirazi (Iranian cucumber, tomato and onion salad)
steps: Dice the cucumbers, tomatoes and onion into small, even cubes and combine them in a bowl.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, dried mint, salt and pepper together.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables just before serving to keep them crisp.
Toss gently and serve alongside kebabs and rice.

title: Sholezard (Iranian saffron rice pudding)

ingredients.name: pinch of saffron, ground and steeped in 4 tbsp hot water

steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it in the water, partly covered, for about 45 minutes until very soft and starting to break down.
Stir in the sugar and cook for 15 more minutes, stirring often so it does not stick.
Add the saffron water and butter and cook until the pudding is thick and glossy.
Stir in the rosewater and take it off the heat.
Spoon into dishes and decorate with cinnamon, almonds and pistachios. Serve chilled or at room temperature.

title: Tahchin (Iranian saffron yogurt rice cake with chicken)

ingredients.name: saffron, ground and steeped in 3 tbsp hot water

steps: Simmer the chicken with the onion, turmeric, salt and pepper in a little water for 25 minutes, then shred or slice it.
Parboil the rice for 6 minutes in salted water and drain well.
Mix the yogurt, egg yolks, half the saffron water and a few tablespoons of melted butter, then fold in two-thirds of the rice.
Spread this saffron rice in a buttered ovenproof dish, pressing it up the sides.
Layer the chicken in the middle, cover with the remaining plain rice, drizzle with saffron water and remaining butter, and cover with foil.
Bake at 180 C for about 1 hour 15 minutes until the base is golden and firm, rest for 10 minutes, and invert onto a plate to serve.
